scope: Finite documentary decision grid of sufficient source hypotheses, not exhaustive literature or global MLC proof. open = no fully audited covering implication in this cell; may contain covered points or be empty. Reported preprints kept separate. Tests include source-defined geometric conditions and not all are decidable from finite words.

Y.author: J.-C. Yoccoz (Hubbard exposition)
Y.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets and bifurcation loci: three theorems of J.-C. Yoccoz
hypotheses: c in M
not infinitely renormalizable
Y.conclusion: Basis of connected relative neighborhoods in M.

L.author: M. Lyubich
L.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
L.locator: Rigidity Theorem and Cor. 1.1 p. 187; §2.5 pp. 198–199; Thm IV' p. 239
hypotheses: SL: all straightened renormalizations in a fixed finite collection of truncated secondary limbs
a priori bounds on renormalizations; rigidity applies to maps satisfying these hypotheses
for high-period route IV': SL, sufficiently large relative periods at every level, accumulation set of arbitrarily long central cascades contains no parabolic or Siegel maps
L.conclusion: At most one map satisfying SL and bounds in a combinatorial class; to infer singleton fiber must control the whole class. IV' supplies bounds under its additional assumptions.

Lreal.author: M. Lyubich
Lreal.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
hypotheses: real infinitely renormalizable quadratic
all essential periods of renormalizations > universal p

Ldensity.author: M. Lyubich
Ldensity.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials, I–II
hypotheses: real quadratics
Ldensity.conclusion: Real rigidity/density of hyperbolicity; not a complex-fiber MLC theorem by itself.

K.author: J. Kahn
K.title: A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: I. Bounded primitive combinatorics
hypotheses: infinite sequence of primitive renormalizations with absolute periods p_k
p_(k+1)/p_k bounded uniformly
K.conclusion: A priori bounds and parameter rigidity/MLC via Lyubich; a cofinal absolute-primitive sequence is the test, not just a claim that some relative levels are primitive.

KLdec.author: J. Kahn and M. Lyubich
KLdec.title: A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics: II. Decorations
KLdec.locator: Main Theorem and Cor. 1.1, p. 58; Thm 1.2 p. 59; §2.1
hypotheses: infinite sequence of primitive combinatorics
relative copies contained in a fixed finite family of decorations in the sense of §2.1
KLdec.conclusion: A priori bounds and MLC at the parameter.

KLmol.author: J. Kahn and M. Lyubich
KLmol.title: A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratics, III: Molecules
KLmol.venue: Complex Dynamics: Families and Friends (2009), 229–256; author preprint IMS07-04
KLmol.locator: Main Theorem p. 1; Cor. 1.1 p. 2; §2.2 pp. 5–6 (preprint)
hypotheses: infinite primitive renormalization sequence
relative types uniformly separated from the main molecule by some eta>0, in source combinatorial sense (uniform r,q,n of §2.2)

DL23.author: D. Dudko and M. Lyubich
DL23.title: Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set at some satellite parameters of bounded type
hypotheses: periodic point c(theta) of the molecule renormalization on the main cardioid boundary
small copy M_0 near that point as constructed in the theorem
inverse orbit of M_0 for the periodic return of molecule renormalization (the source's stationary satellite construction)
DL23.conclusion: Nested copies shrink; combinatorial rigidity and local connectivity at the constructed satellite parameters. Not all bounded satellite types.

DL26.author: D. Dudko and M. Lyubich
DL26.title: MLC at Feigenbaum points
DL26.locator: Theorems A and B p. 3, definitions pp. 2–3, §2.2.5 (arXiv)
hypotheses: infinitely quadratic-like renormalizable
uniform finite upper bound on relative periods p_(n+1)/p_n
DL26.conclusion: A priori bounds and MLC at all bounded-type Feigenbaum parameters, no all-primitive or all-satellite restriction.

CS.author: D. Cheraghi and M. Shishikura
CS.title: Satellite renormalization of quadratic polynomials
CS.locator: Theorem D p. 6; signed continued fractions pp. 5–6; (6.8) and example p. 62
hypotheses: all levels satellite, reduced fractions a_i/q_i
signed continued fractions with digits b_i,j and signs epsilon_i,j as defined in source
b_1,1 >= N for theorem threshold N; b_i,j+1 >= b_i,j^2; b_i+1,1 >= q_i^2
CS.conclusion: Exponential shrinking of nested Mandelbrot copies and MLC. For one-digit rotations ±1/q_i: q_1 >= N and q_(i+1) >= q_i^2. Mere high digits are insufficient.

C.author: D. Cheraghi
C.title: Combinatorial rigidity for some infinitely renormalizable unicritical polynomials
hypotheses: infinitely renormalizable unicritical maps
secondary limbs condition
a priori bounds for maps compared
C.conclusion: Combinatorial rigidity under these geometric hypotheses; not an independent high-type satellite theorem.

Lev1.author: G. Levin
Lev1.title: Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials
hypotheses: sequence of absolute simple-renormalization periods n_m
limsup log |p_m| / n_m > 0 for numerators of dividing rotation; or satellite subsequence with limsup log q_m / n_m > 0

Lev2.author: G. Levin
Lev2.title: Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials
hypotheses: infinite satellite cascade with denominators q_m tending to infinity
limsup |t_(m+1)|^(1/q_m) < 1
Lev2.conclusion: MLC at limit; Julia set not locally connected.

Levadd.author: G. Levin
Levadd.title: Addendum to Rigidity and non-local connectivity of Julia sets of some quadratic polynomials
Levadd.venue: Commun. Math. Phys. (2014), 1171 ff.; Addendum included in arXiv:0710.4406v4
hypotheses: satellite cascade, t_m=p_m/q_m
sup_(m>=1) |t_m| product_(k=0..m-1) q_k < infinity
limsup q_m/(product_(k=0..m-1) q_k)^2 > 0

EE.author: J. Kahn and M. Lyubich
EE.title: A priori bounds for some infinitely renormalizable quadratic: IV. Elephant Eyes
EE.locator: §4.0.1 E1–E3 p. 9; MLC statement §8 p. 18 (unnumbered; proof not audited)
hypotheses: primitive elephant-eye relative types at every relevant level
dividing rotation 1/q; central Y contains only the central little filled Julia set; relative period q+b with b uniformly bounded
source uses b<q simplification
EE.conclusion: A priori bounds; MLC application stated in §8 with additional cited rigidity inputs; application proof assigned to separate research thread.

KKL.author: J. Kahn, A. Kapiamba and M. Lyubich
KKL.title: MLC for parabolically bounded primitive renormalization
KKL.locator: Theorems A,B p. 3; C p. 4; reference DKLP p. 71
hypotheses: infinite prime primitive renormalization types from a parabolically bounded family in source definition
finite union of individual types and parabolic tails via source Branner–Douady embeddings Phi_q of fixed primitive type
Theorem B separately requires beau bounds and bounded puzzle Teichmüller diameter
KKL.conclusion: Theorem C states MLC for this family; its rigidity chain uses DKLP in preparation. Not general primitive or mixed renormalization. The remark after C explicitly puts mixed bounded satellite/primitive-parabolic tails combination outside the article's scope.

LY.author: M. Lyubich and M. Yampolsky
LY.title: Dynamics of quadratic polynomials: complex bounds for real maps
LY.locator: Theorem 1.1, Complex Bounds Theorem and Local Connectivity Theorem p. 1220
hypotheses: real infinitely renormalizable quadratic
Theorem 1.1 essential periods bounded; exception finite final doubling near cusp; combined theorem universal bounds
LY.conclusion: A priori bounds and JLC for real quadratics, not a general MLC theorem.

LvS.author: G. Levin and S. van Strien
LvS.title: Local connectivity of the Julia set of real polynomials
hypotheses: real polynomials in specified class; applies to real quadratics
LvS.conclusion: Julia set local connectivity, not complex parameter-plane MLC.

GS.author: J. Graczyk and G. Świątek
GS.title: Generic hyperbolicity in the logistic family
hypotheses: real logistic family; precise journal theorem UNVERIFIED
GS.conclusion: Real density result; no imported MLC implication here.

DKL.author: D. Dudko, J. Kahn and M. Lyubich
DKL.title: Local connectivity of the Mandelbrot set along the real line
DKL.venue: Manuscript (2022), cited as [14] by Dudko survey
DKL.locator: UNVERIFIED primary manuscript; survey §4.3 after Theorem 4.1 and ref. [14]
hypotheses: real line and veins as reported by survey; exact primary hypotheses UNVERIFIED
DKL.conclusion: Survey reports all-real and vein MLC. Not an independently verified primary theorem in this atlas.

survey.author: D. Dudko
survey.title: On the MLC Conjecture and the Renormalization Theory in Complex Dynamics
survey.locator: HTML v1 https://arxiv.org/html/2512.24171v1; §4.2–4.5, Thm 4.1/4.2, Problems 4.3/4.4; PDF page UNVERIFIED
hypotheses: exposition and open problems
survey.conclusion: Bounded-type coverage; remaining unbounded satellite bounds and virtual molecule interpolation. Not an additional independent MLC theorem.

TUN.author: D. Schleicher
TUN.title: On Fibers and Renormalization of Julia Sets and Multibrot Sets
TUN.locator: Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2, p. 6 (IMS PDF); Introduction p. 2
hypotheses: finite tuning homeomorphism of Multibrot set onto a little copy
trivial parameter fiber of the untuned point
TUN.conclusion: Trivial fibers preserved in both directions under every tuning map, hence MLC for a tuned trivial-fiber point. Not a new base case.

grid.rotation_definition: For satellite levels only: standard nearest-integer signed CF after mod 1 representative in (-1/2,1/2]; bounded means uniform bound on all digits; otherwise distinguish minimum digit at satellite levels tends to infinity or does not (for finitely many satellite levels use bounded). High type = every digit >= a threshold N, separately record that flag; can coexist with bounded digits. Unbounded relative periods need not mean unbounded CF digits (long fractions).

excluded.reason: Real satellite copies have rotation 1/2, relative period 2 at every level.

k.test: cofinal absolute primitive renormalizations with bounded ratios of their absolute periods; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

dec.test: source's primitive finite decoration condition; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

mol.test: source's primitive uniform anti-molecule condition; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

real_essential.test: some straightened tail is real and all of its essential periods exceed the threshold of Theorem VIII (or the original parameter satisfies that hypothesis)

qg.test: all-satellite signed CF quadratic growth QG_N; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

levin1.test: source's simple-renormalization exponential numerator or satellite denominator criterion; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

levin2.test: source's all-satellite exponential next-rotation criterion; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

levinadd.test: source's all-satellite addendum product conditions; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

ee.test: source's E1–E3 elephant-eye family; allow a finite tail only if the theorem establishes a singleton parameter fiber, then use TUN

grid.semantics: First true applicable predicate, allowing finite tails when the original theorem establishes a trivial parameter fiber (nested copies shrink or equivalent); Schleicher Cor. 3.2 transfers triviality under any finite tuning. Tests are source statements, not just coarse regime labels. The real_essential test includes a real straightened tail, not merely original locus. For EE/KKL, stated preprint applications remain separately tagged. Residual means all earlier applicable tests false. An all-real/vein manuscript is reported, not independently source-verified.

example.order: Within nonreal-at-first-step, positive numerator-one affine strictly increasing denominator words q_i=a+b(i-1), integers a>=3,b>=1, order lexicographically by (b,a); (1,3) is minimum. Not absolute minimum over all words or all open subclasses.
example.proof: Nested tuned satellite copies are nonempty compact. A member of their intersection has the specified infinite cascade; first upper 1/3 limb excludes real locus. No singleton or parameter LC asserted.

checks.Y: Infinitely many satellite levels, not finitely renormalizable.
checks.L: Unbounded first-limb denominators 3,4,... cannot lie in a fixed finite family of truncated secondary limbs. No class-wide bounds established; IV' SL also fails.
checks.Ldensity: Nonreal; density alone is not MLC.
checks.K: No primitive absolute renormalization in the pure satellite cascade.
checks.KLdec: No primitive levels, lies in satellite molecule rather than finite decorations.
checks.KLmol: All relative copies satellite attached to main cardioid, not uniformly away from molecule.
checks.DL23: Unbounded relative periods, not stationary bounded satellite construction.
checks.CS: Single signed digit q_i; q_(i+1)=q_i+1<q_i^2 at every level; eventual high type does not give QG_N.
checks.C: SL fails by unbounded denominators; no class-wide a priori bounds.
checks.Lev1: Numerator 1 gives log 1=0; log q_i divided by prior absolute period tends to zero; same for every subsequence (a later rotation in a simple satellite level is its own q_i).
checks.Levadd: Product prior q_j divided by q_i diverges, and q_i divided by squared prior product tends to zero.
checks.EE: Relative types are satellite, not primitive E1–E3.
checks.KKL: Relative types satellite, not prime primitive.
checks.GS: Nonreal; journal theorem UNVERIFIED, not an MLC implication.
checks.DKL: Nonreal and no claim to lie on a specified vein; primary manuscript unavailable, cannot rule out unspecified extension.
checks.survey: Consistent with remaining unbounded satellite Problem 4.3; 4.4 concerns virtual primitive levels, not this word.
checks.TUN: Every finite tail has the same slow growth and none of the audited base hypotheses, so finite tuning of a certified trivial-fiber point is not supplied. This transfer cannot itself establish the tail.

survey_comparison.match: Problem 4.3 (§4.4) remaining unbounded satellite ql bounds; explicit slow pure-satellite example falls in this direction of research.
survey_comparison.not_match: Problem 4.4 (§4.5) virtual near-Molecule interpolation of primitive maximal copies. No discrepancy found; 2026 preprints postdate survey.
survey_comparison.real: Survey §4.3 reports real/vein result in manuscript [14]. Do not conflate with old real JLC and density theorems.
survey_comparison.limits: Neither survey nor this search proves that no later theorem covers the explicit word. No global minimality, no claim of non-MLC.
